sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Economic Distress**: The war led to heavy taxation, rising prices, and export of food grains, causing widespread **famine and inflation**.
• **Global Context**: The **Self-Determination** principle (Wilson’s 14 Points) and the Russian Revolution (1917) inspired Indian nationalists to demand political rights.
• **Institutional Shift**: The **Lucknow Pact (1916)** marked the reunion of Moderates and Extremists and the Congress-League alliance, creating a unified front.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The **Home Rule League Movement** (Tilak and Besant) acted as the primary vehicle for political agitation during the war years.

Pan-India (Tilak: Maharashtra/Karnataka; Besant: Rest of India)
Demand for 'Self-Government' within the British Empire

items.definition: A landmark agreement between INC and Muslim League; accepted separate electorates, marking the peak of Hindu-Muslim unity.
Montagu’s statement promising 'responsible government' in India, aimed at pacifying nationalists during the war.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **War Effort Support**: Gandhi initially supported the British war effort, hoping for post-war reforms.
• **Revolutionary Terrorism**: The Berlin Committee and the Indo-German conspiracy attempted to smuggle arms into India.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Severe repression via Defence of India Act (1915).
• **Solutions**: Shift toward non-violent mass movements (Satyagraha) post-1917.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'L-H-A-G' (Lucknow, Home Rule, August Declaration, Ghadar).
• **Decoded Meaning**: L (1916 Unity), H (1916 Agitation), A (1917 Policy), G (1913-15 Revolutionary).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 'August Declaration' (1917) with the 'August Offer' (1940). Remember: 1917 is Montagu (WWI), 1940 is Linlithgow (WWII).
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Political Awakening' to describe how the war transformed the Indian middle class from petitioners to agitators.

keyTakeaways: The war acted as a catalyst for the unification of the Congress and the Muslim League.
The Home Rule Movement provided the organizational structure for future Gandhian movements.
The British promise of 'responsible government' in 1917 was a strategic concession to maintain wartime stability.
